title: SQL Set 01: Core HCL Payroll & Employee Queries
description: Reported HCLTech SQL interview and coding round staples: top-N salaries, second highest salary, department averages, joins, and duplicate detection.

queries.title: Top 3 Highest-Paid Employees
queries.prompt: Write a SQL query to return the `emp_name`, `dept`, and `salary` of the top 3 highest-paid employees, ordered by `salary` descending and `emp_id` ascending on ties.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE employees (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INT, email TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT emp_name, dept, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC LIMIT 3;
queries.explanation: Sort descending by `salary` with a deterministic tie-breaker (`emp_id ASC`) before applying `LIMIT 3`.

queries.title: Employees Earning Above Department Average
queries.prompt: Retrieve `emp_id`, `emp_name`, `dept`, and `salary` for every employee whose `salary` is strictly greater than the average salary of their own department. Order by `emp_id` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE staff (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT s.emp_id, s.emp_name, s.dept, s.salary FROM staff s JOIN (SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM staff GROUP BY dept) d ON s.dept = d.dept WHERE s.salary > d.avg_sal ORDER BY s.emp_id;
queries.explanation: Compute per-department average in a derived table (or window `AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept)`) and keep only rows strictly exceeding it (Tara equals her 1-person department average, so excluded).

queries.title: Second Highest Distinct Salary
queries.prompt: Find the second highest distinct salary from the `payroll` table as column `second_highest_salary`. Ensure tied top salaries do not hide the true second highest salary.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE payroll (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, salary INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary FROM payroll WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM payroll);
queries.explanation: `WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM payroll)` handles duplicate max values and safely returns NULL if fewer than 2 distinct salaries exist.

queries.title: Detect Duplicate Email Records
queries.prompt: Find all `email` values that appear more than once in `candidates`, along with their occurrence count as `dup_count`. Order alphabetically by `email`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE candidates (cand_id INT PRIMARY KEY, full_name TEXT, email TEXT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO candidates VALUES (1,'Riya Sen','riya@mail.com'),(2,'Aman Roy','aman@mail.com'),(3,'Riya S','riya@mail.com'),(4,'Karan Das','karan@mail.com'),(5,'Aman R','aman@mail.com'),(6,'Aman K','aman@mail.com');
queries.solutionSql: SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS dup_count FROM candidates GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY email;
queries.explanation: Group rows by `email` and filter post-aggregation using `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`.

queries.title: Join Departments and Compute Headcount & Total Payroll
queries.prompt: Join `departments` and `emp_roster` to return `dept_name`, `headcount`, and `total_salary` (0 if a department has no employees). Order by `total_salary` descending, then `dept_name` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE departments (dept_id INT PRIMARY KEY, dept_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE emp_roster (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, dept_id INT, salary INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO departments VALUES (10,'Platform'),(20,'Data'),(30,'Security'); INSERT INTO emp_roster VALUES (1,'A',10,80000),(2,'B',10,95000),(3,'C',20,105000);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS headcount, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0) AS total_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN emp_roster e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY total_salary DESC, d.dept_name ASC;
queries.explanation: Use `LEFT JOIN` to keep Security (0 employees), `COUNT(e.emp_id)` instead of `COUNT(*)` so NULL rows count as 0, and `COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0)`.
